source: Morais O., Cargill C., Parke K. and Barnes T. 2020. Smallholder Pig Production Technicians' Manual. Timor-Leste Ministry of Agriculture and Fisheries, University of Queensland, ACIAR and the TOMAK Program (Australian Aid), Dili.
text: Golden/water snails (a common rice-paddy pest) are a cheap animal-protein source for pigs — feed them fresh, shell and all, at a rate of about 400g fresh snails per 1kg of dry feed mix, twice daily. To raise snails in a purpose-built pond: dig a hole 60–100cm deep in a spot with year-round water access; wall the sides with concrete or leave as soil/mud; surround the pond with a rice-husk layer (30–50cm) then a sand layer (30–50cm) to stop snails escaping, and cover the whole area with fine netting (like mosquito net); build a shade roof from coconut or palm leaves; add water, cow manure, and soil and let it settle 1–2 weeks before adding snails collected from rice fields or rivers; place sticks in the pond for the snails to lay eggs on; feed the colony leaves, manure, and rice bran every 2 days; and change the water every 2–4 weeks, keeping it below 31°C. Because snails are a genuine pest to rice farmers, ponds must be secured to prevent any escape into surrounding fields.
caveat: This guidance comes from a Timor-Leste smallholder pig manual, not a Cambodia-specific source. Feed ingredients and general husbandry practices transfer well to Cambodia's tropical smallholder conditions, but local breed weights/ages and disease-context details may differ; confirm specifics with a local vet or extension officer where precision matters.
